tags.name: Introduction
tags.description:
This API allows ChatGPT Enterprise administrators to observe and remove data from their ChatGPT Enterprise workspaces. It is intended for compliance, security, and data privacy use. The delete endpoints are designed for spot deletion of data, not bulk deletion. Administrators can use it to retrieve this data for archival or Data Loss Prevention purposes as part of a compliance or security program.
The OpenAI Programmatic Admin Platform organizes documentation into three sections: - **Compliance Log Platform** for immutable, append-only compliance log events for auditing purposes. - **Admin API administration** for stateful workspace administration, export, and spot-deletion endpoints. - **Analytics** for workspace, cost, and Codex analytics reporting APIs. Use this API for compliance, security, and data governance workflows. The delete endpoints are designed for spot deletions, while list/get endpoints are intended for recurring sync jobs rather than one-time full exports. ### Authentication Workspace owners and workspace admins can create workspace-scoped Admin keys in the [OpenAI Admin Console](https://admin.openai.com/credentials?tab=admin-keys) under **Credentials > Admin keys**. Select the workspace and use **Restricted** permissions whenever possible. Workspace owners can create Restricted, Read only, or All permissions keys, including sensitive Compliance API scopes when they are available for the workspace; workspace admins can create Restricted keys only for permitted non-sensitive scopes. Copy the secret immediately because it is shown only once, store it securely, and send requests with `Authorization: Bearer `. Use `https://api.chatgpt.com/v1/` as the base URL for all endpoints. ### Retention Deleted data is not recoverable. This API does not provide deletion of OpenAI internal audit or security logs. Authenticated requests are logged for security/compliance and deleted content is removed from internal search/retrieval indexes. Data is retained internally for no greater than 30 days after a deletion request. #### **Messages** There are several ways messages can be edited/deleted in ChatGPT: - Workspace setting: Admins can set a retention setting for the entire workspace (minimum 90d). Messages will be deleted N days after the last edit to the conversation (N set by Admins) on a going forward basis. - User delete conversation: These conversations will still be available via this API for up to 30d but not visible to the user. - User edit/delete message: These conversations will be shown via the API in the conversation tree subject to the retention settings above #### **Files** There are 4 different file retentions within ChatGPT: - GPT & Project Files: Files uploaded to GPTs/Projects are retained indefinitely since new conversations require them. - Chat Uploaded Files: Files uploaded by users are held temporarily (48hrs) - Generated Files: Files generated by ChatGPT (ie DALLE) are held based on the workspace's retention setting ### File URL Expiration File URLs are generated each time the Compliance API is polled. - Files can be downloaded from these URLs, and for security reasons, they have an expiry of 1 hour. - For direct requests to fetch file contents, the redirect contains an ephemeral download URL which expires after 5 minutes. - Thus, if files are needed for compliance purposes, messages should be polled regularly (before their retention setting) and then downloaded soon after polling before the URL expires.

tags.name: Compliance Logs Platform
tags.description:
### Overview
The Compliance Logs Platform is a simple and reliable way to export enterprise observability and compliance data.
Instead of polling many object endpoints, you download immutable, time‑windowed JSONL files for the data categories you are interested in (e.g., conversation messages, audit logs).
These files are generated frequently and are designed for low‑latency ingestion into your SIEM, data lake, or e‑discovery tooling.

#### Key Attributes
- Simple File API that delivers immutable JSONL files grouped by data type.
- Minutes‑level target latency and improved reliability via a modernized pipeline.
- Files expire after a 30d retention window. Consumers should regularly ingest data and retain as necessary for their use-cases.
- Latency SLA of a p99 of <30min from event time to inclusion in a log file
- Logs contain the value of the data at the time of the event - not at the time of ingestion.
This ensures you have access to all data for audit purposes - even if it only existed transiently.

### Authentication
For broad read access to all log types, create an Admin API key with the
`chatgpt.enterprise.compliance_logs_platform.read` scope. In the Admin portal
**Create Admin API key** modal, the scope is displayed as
**Compliance logging platform** > **Read**.

The legacy `chatgpt.enterprise.compliance_export.read` scope remains supported
for backward compatibility, but new integrations should use
`chatgpt.enterprise.compliance_logs_platform.read`. You can alternatively grant
the fine-grained read scope documented for each log type.


### How it works
- Files are immutable once written.
- OpenAI retains files for a limited duration.
  If retention is desired then consumers should implement a system to continuously download all files and retain them according to their policies.
- File names reflect the write time; the contract is that each file contains events with timestamps up to (and including)
  that write time.
- Late events (within SLA) may appear in a later file. Plan ingestion to accept such late arrivals.
- Events are handled with an "at least once" contract and so duplicates may appear across files.
  Always de‑duplicate using the stable `event_id`.
- Files are produced on a regular cadence (~10‑minute windows) and are grouped by type (e.g., `AUDIT_LOG`, `AUTH_LOG`, `CODEX_LOG`, `CHATGPT_PLUGIN_SPREADSHEET`, etc).
  Each file is capped at 15MB and any logs within the time window after that cap will start a new file and time window.


### Getting started
1. List the files for the `event_type`s and time range you care about (likely the time from last ingestion to time of pull). Download each file; parse as JSONL.
Checkout the [Compliance Logs Platform quickstart](https://cookbook.openai.com/examples/chatgpt/compliance_api/logs_platform) for example scripts to get started quickly.
3. De‑duplicate across files using `event_id`.
4. Persist to your store and checkpoint by last reported time
5. Handle rate‑limits with backoff and retry

### Base schema
Each event conforms to the shared Logs Platform envelope with the following top-level fields:

- `event_id`: Stable identifier for the event.
- `type`: `event_type` for the file.
- `timestamp`: ISO 8601 timestamp (UTC) for when the action completed.
- `principal`: Object describing the principal account that this action belongs to.
  - `id`: Principal ID
  - `type`: Currently `"CHATGPT_WORKSPACE"` or `"API_PLATFORM_ORG"`.
- `actor`: Object describing who initiated the action.
  - Account user actor:
    - `type`: `"ACCOUNT_USER"`.
    - `user_id`: ChatGPT user ID of the actor.
    - `user_email`: Email address of the actor.
    - `credential_id`: Stable, non-secret identifier for the personal access token
      that authenticated the actor, when the action was PAT-authenticated.
  - Compliance API key actor:
    - `type`: `"API_KEY"`.
    - `redacted_id`: Redacted key identifier in the form `xxx...yyyy` (first 3 and last 4 characters).

### Best practices
- Always dedupe on `event_id`; do not assume strict partitioning by window boundaries.
- Expect late arrivals within the SLA window; design your analytics to accommodate them.
- Download generated assets using provided URLs if needed; binaries are not embedded in JSON.

### Migration and compatibility
- The Logs Platform does not support self-service backfilling historical data and instead focuses on forward-moving data.
- To help with their compliance requirements, customers can take advantage of Compliance API integrations built by leading eDiscovery and Data Loss Prevention (DLP) companies.
See our [Help Center](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/9261474-compliance-api-for-enterprise-customers#partner-integrations) for details.

tags.name: Conversation Messages
tags.description:
This section describes conversation message log files available through the OpenAI Compliance Logs Platform.

`event_type` = `CONVERSATION_MESSAGE`
Fine-grained API key scope: `chatgpt.enterprise.compliance_logs_platform.conversation_message.read`.
API keys with `chatgpt.enterprise.compliance_logs_platform.read` or the legacy
`chatgpt.enterprise.compliance_export.read` scope can also read Conversation Messages.

### Overview
Each `CONVERSATION_MESSAGE` entry is an immutable snapshot of one message in a conversation.
This enables you to have access to data for audit purposes - even if it only existed transiently.
If you wish to reconstruct the conversations, then retain events and group them by `conversation.id` using `previous_message_id` to determine message order.

### Schema
Each event conforms to the shared Logs Platform envelope described above with these additional top-level fields:
- `type`: Always `CONVERSATION_MESSAGE`.
- `previous_message_id`: The `message.id` of the last message before this one in the conversation. Omitted for the first message.
- `message`: Object with the details of the message.
  - `id`: Stable identifier
  - `created_at`: ISO 8601 timestamp for when the message was created, when available. The top-level `timestamp` remains the event/action time, so the same `message.id` may appear in multiple events if the message is updated.
  - `author`: One of the following author variants (discriminated by `type`):
    - `user: { type: "user", client_type: string }`

      Human user message made by the `actor` listed in the base Logs Platform envelope. `client_type` is always present and describes the client surface associated with the message. Possible values are `unknown`, `desktop_web`, `ios_web`, `ios_app`, `macos_app`, `windows_app`, `android_web`, `android_app`, and `chatgpt_api`.
    - `assistant: { type: "assistant", model: string, tools_used?: string[], skills_used?: string[] }`

      Model-authored message; `model` is always present (e.g. `gpt-5-2-pro`), `tools_used` lists any assistant tools invoked for the response when available, and `skills_used` lists skill IDs associated with the message when available.
  - `content`: Optional object describing the message payload. Each content object has a `type` discriminator and is one of:
    - `text: { type: "text", value?: string, annotations?: Annotation[] }`

      Standard user/assistant text; `value` may be null when no displayable text exists, and `annotations` add structured references.
      - `annotations`: One of:
        - `url_citation: { type: "url_citation", urls: string[] }`

          URLs cited in the text.
        - `file_citation: { type: "file_citation", files: { id, name }[] }`

          Files referenced in the text by id/name.
        - `custom_action: { type: "custom_action", action_domain: string, action_name: string }`

          Custom action metadata tied to the text.
    - `user_instructions: { type: "user_instructions", value: string }`

      Instructional content provided by a user to guide the assistant.
    - `quotation: { type: "quotation", file_id?: string, file_name?: string, quote?: string }`

      A snippet quoted from a user-uploaded file; file fields may be null if unavailable.
  - `files`: Optional list of files attached to the message, each containing `id` and `name`.
- `conversation`: Object describing the conversation the message is a part of.
  - `id`: Conversation ID (string).
  - `title`: Conversation title (string).
  - `gpt_id`: GPT ID string when the conversation is with a GPT.
  - `gpt_name`: GPT name string provided when available.
  - `project_id`: Project ID string when the conversation is within a Project.
  - `project_name`: Project name string provided when available.
  - `created_at`: ISO 8601 timestamp for conversation creation (string or null).
  - `is_pinned`, `is_temporary_chat`: Flags of if the named state was true at the time of the event.

### Example
```json
{
  "event_id": "9d6bb4e9-3882-4dbe-9d4c-2668b692f9f1",
  "type": "CONVERSATION_MESSAGE",
  "timestamp": "2025-05-13T18:22:11.902144Z",
  "previous_message_id": "msg-122",
  "principal": {
    "id": "be545252-ad04-4cfa-9ca5-deca58416151",
    "type": "CHATGPT_WORKSPACE"
  },
  "actor": {
    "type": "ACCOUNT_USER",
    "user_id": "user-AbCdEf1234567890",
    "user_email": "user@example.org"
  },
  "message": {
    "id": "msg-123",
    "author": {
      "type": "assistant",
      "model": "gpt-4.1",
      "tools_used": ["browser"],
      "skills_used": ["skill-123"]
    },
    "content": {
      "type": "text",
      "value": "Here are the sources.",
      "annotations": [
        {
          "type": "url_citation",
          "urls": ["https://example.org"]
        }
      ]
    },
    "files": [
      {
        "id": "file-123",
        "name": "report.pdf"
      }
    ]
  },
  "conversation": {
    "id": "convo-456",
    "title": "Quarterly review",
    "gpt_id": "g-abcdef",
    "created_at": "2025-05-13T17:59:02Z"
  }
}
```

### Historical rehydration assistance
For ongoing compliance requirements, customers should continuously ingest and retain any Compliance Logs Platform files they may need, because files expire after the 30d retention window.
If historical `CONVERSATION_MESSAGE` events are needed after that window has passed, support can assist with a replay as a fallback, such as when first setting up a CLP integration or responding to an incident.
Email [support@openai.com](mailto:support@openai.com) requesting a "Compliance Logs Platform rehydration of CONVERSATION_MESSAGE logs" with the requested timeframe and any specific relevant user IDs.

tags.name: Apps
tags.description:
This section describes the App invocation log files and their format as available through the OpenAI Compliance Logs Platform.

Each APP_LOG entry corresponds to either the request into a app tool or the response returned by that App.
A single invocation typically produces two events: one with `log_type = "request"` and one with `log_type = "response"` (the response may be omitted if a failure prevents a result from being generated).

`event_type` = `APP_LOG`
Fine-grained API key scope: `chatgpt.enterprise.compliance_logs_platform.app_log.read`.
API keys with `chatgpt.enterprise.compliance_logs_platform.read` or the legacy
`chatgpt.enterprise.compliance_export.read` scope can also read Apps.

### Schema
Each event conforms to the shared Logs Platform envelope described above with these additional top‑level fields:
- `type`: Always `APP_LOG`.
- `app_id`: Stable identifier of the App configuration (string).
- `app_name`: Human‑readable name of the App at invocation time (string).
- `app_type`: Classification of the App backend. Possible values: `SERVICE` (service‑backed connector such as Google or Microsoft), `OPEN_API` (OpenAPI‑defined connector), `MCP` (connector backed by an MCP server), `FIRST_PARTY_ECOSYSTEM` (first‑party ecosystem connector), `UNKNOWN` (type not captured).
- `conversation_id`: Conversation identifier related to the invocation (string, nullable) – may be `null` for background or system initiated calls.
- `log_type`: Indicates whether the event captures the `request` or the `response` phase. Possible values: `request`, `response`.
- `input`: Object containing the request payload sent to the app (present on `request` events; may be omitted or `null` on `response`).
- `output`: Array of objects containing the normalized response items returned by the app (present on `response` events; omitted on `request`).

Additional app‑specific keys may appear; they should be treated as informational and are subject to change. Always rely only on the documented fields above for stable ingestion.

### Example (request)
```json
{
  "event_id": "31c1b9b0-5b2d-4c2a-9e11-32d7b0c3e9aa",
  "type": "APP_LOG",
  "timestamp": "2025-11-15T20:12:24.551203Z",
  "principal": {
    "id": "be545252-ad04-4cfa-9ca5-deca58416151",
    "type": "CHATGPT_WORKSPACE"
  },
  "actor": {
    "type": "ACCOUNT_USER",
    "user_id": "user-AbCdEf1234567890",
    "user_email": "user@example.org"
  },
  "app_id": "conn-8f92d7c1",
  "app_name": "gdrive",
  "app_type": "SERVICE",
  "conversation_id": "c-7cda9b2e",
  "log_type": "request",
  "input": {
    "query": "List recent architecture decisions"
  }
}
```

### Example (response)
```json
{
  "event_id": "31c1b9b0-5b2d-4c2a-9e11-32d7b0c3e9ab",
  "type": "APP_LOG",
  "timestamp": "2025-11-15T20:12:25.012944Z",
  "principal": {
    "id": "be545252-ad04-4cfa-9ca5-deca58416151",
    "type": "CHATGPT_WORKSPACE"
  },
  "actor": {
    "type": "ACCOUNT_USER",
    "user_id": "user-AbCdEf1234567890",
    "user_email": "user@example.org"
  },
  "app_id": "conn-8f92d7c1",
  "app_name": "gdrive",
  "app_type": "SERVICE",
  "conversation_id": "c-7cda9b2e",
  "log_type": "response",
  "output": [
    {"display_title": "ADR-017 Caching Strategy", "display_url": "https://confluence.example.org/x/Qw12"},
    {"display_title": "ADR-016 Messaging Bus", "display_url": "https://confluence.example.org/x/Rx34"}
  ]
}
```

tags.name: Apps Auth
tags.description:
This section describes app auth lifecycle log files (link/unlink) as available through the OpenAI Compliance Logs Platform.

Each app auth log entry corresponds to a change in authentication linkage for a app (user linking a app credential, or unlinking it).

`event_type` = `APP_AUTH_LOG`
Fine-grained API key scope: `chatgpt.enterprise.compliance_logs_platform.app_auth_log.read`.
API keys with `chatgpt.enterprise.compliance_logs_platform.read` or the legacy
`chatgpt.enterprise.compliance_export.read` scope can also read Apps Auth.

### Schema
Each event conforms to the shared Logs Platform envelope with these additional top‑level fields:
- `type`: Always `APP_AUTH_LOG`.
- `app_id`: Identifier of the app whose auth state changed (nullable string). This may be `null` on unlink if the app record was removed prior to event emission.
- `link_id`: Stable identifier for the specific auth linkage instance (string).
- `action`: Auth lifecycle action performed. Possible values: `link` = Connected, `unlink` = Disconnected.

No additional nested objects are guaranteed; treat unknown extra keys as non‑contract / informational.

### Example (link)
```json
{
  "event_id": "7b3e4de1-2219-4d6c-9d6e-8f4d40c7c001",
  "type": "APP_AUTH_LOG",
  "timestamp": "2025-11-15T20:33:11.112450Z",
  "principal": {
    "id": "be545252-ad04-4cfa-9ca5-deca58416151",
    "type": "CHATGPT_WORKSPACE"
  },
  "actor": {
    "type": "ACCOUNT_USER",
    "user_id": "user-AbCdEf1234567890",
    "user_email": "user@example.org"
  },
  "app_id": "conn-8f92d7c1",
  "link_id": "link-52c0e6b7",
  "action": "link"
}
```

tags.name: Audit
tags.description:
This section describes the Audit Log files and their format as available through the OpenAI Compliance Logs Platform as described above.

Each audit log entry corresponds to a specific action taken within the system.

`event_type` = `AUDIT_LOG`
Fine-grained API key scope: `chatgpt.enterprise.compliance_logs_platform.audit_log.read`.
API keys with `chatgpt.enterprise.compliance_logs_platform.read` or the legacy
`chatgpt.enterprise.compliance_export.read` scope can also read Audit.

**Note:** Many of these permissions and role changes have been moved to a shared RBAC system.
These logs must be enabled and then are accessible through [API Platform](https://platform.openai.com/docs/api-reference/audit-logs).
Non-RBAC logs are preserved here until the migration is complete.

### Schema
Each event conforms to the shared Logs Platform envelope described above with these additional top-level fields:
- `type`: Always `AUDIT_LOG`.
- `action`: Name of the audit log action.
- `action_result`: Outcome of the action. Possible values: `SUCCESS`, `BLOCKED`, `ERROR`.
- `action_privilege`: Privilege level associated with the action. Possible values: `ADMIN`, `STANDARD_USER`.
- `request_metadata`: Network attributes captured at request time. Keys include:
  - `client_ip`
  - `client_ip_details`
  - `client_user_agent`
  - `client_ja3`
  - `client_ja4`
  - `destination_hostname`
- `action_data`: Object containing action-specific context. Schema varies per `action` and is described below.

### Admin actions
**PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN_REVOKE** — Workspace admin revoked another user's v2 personal access token. The event actor is the admin; `owner_user_id` identifies the token owner.
- `credential_id`: Identifier of the personal access token credential.
- `credential_type`: Credential type; currently `personal_access_token`.
- `credential_name`: User-provided name of the credential.
- `owner_user_id`: Auth user ID of the credential owner.
- `workspace_id`: Workspace in which the credential was issued.
- `expires_at`: Credential expiration time in epoch seconds, or `null` when it does not expire.
- `scopes`: Sorted, deduplicated list of product-access scopes stored on the credential.
- `revoked_at`: Persisted revocation time in epoch seconds, or `null` for a legacy deleted credential without a revocation timestamp.
- `state_changed`: Whether this successful request performed the initial revoke transition.

**APP_ACTIVATE** — Activation of a knowledge app.
- `app_id`: Identifier of the app that was activated.
- `app_name`: Friendly name of the app at the time of activation.

**APP_CREATE** — Creation of a knowledge app.
- `app_id`: Identifier of the new app.
- `knowledge_app_type`: App backend/type that was provisioned.
- `app_name`: Optional friendly name assigned to the app.

**APP_DELETE** — Deletion of a knowledge app.
- `app_id`: Identifier of the app that was removed.
- `app_name`: Friendly name of the app that was removed.

**APP_PUBLISH** — Publication of a knowledge app to end users.
- `app_id`: Identifier of the app that was published.
- `source_surface`: Optional admin surface that initiated the publish; either `admin_apps` or `admin_plugins`.
- `context_plugin_id`: Optional plugin identifier whose UI initiated the publish.
- `affected_connector_ids`: Connector identifiers whose workspace permissions were affected.
- `changed_fields`: Workspace-permission fields changed by the publish.
- `changed_fields_by_connector`: Mapping from connector identifier to fields changed for that connector.
- `previous_workspace_permissions_by_connector`: Mapping from connector identifier to its workspace-permission snapshot before the publish.
- `new_workspace_permissions_by_connector`: Mapping from connector identifier to its workspace-permission snapshot after the publish.

**APP_UPDATE_NAME** — Rename of a knowledge app.
- `app_id`: Identifier of the app that was renamed.
- `old_name`: Previous display name before the change.
- `new_name`: Updated display name.

**APP_ALLOW_USER** — Individual user was granted access to a app.
- `app_id`: Identifier of the app.
- `app_name`: Friendly name of the app.
- `allowed_user_id`: Auth user ID that was granted access.

**APP_DISALLOW_USER** — Individual user access was revoked from a app.
- `app_id`: Identifier of the app.
- `disallowed_user_id`: Auth user ID that lost access.

**APP_UPDATE_ACCESS_POLICY** — Workspace-level access policy change for a app.
- `app_id`: Identifier of the app.
- `app_name`: Friendly name of the app whose policy changed.
- `allow_all_in_workspace`: Whether the app is now visible to the full workspace.

**PLUGIN_UPDATE_INSTALLATION_POLICY** — Updated a workspace plugin installation policy.
- `plugin_id`: Identifier of the plugin whose policy changed.
- `source_surface`: Optional admin surface that initiated the update; currently `admin_plugins`.
- `changed_fields`: Policy fields changed by the update.
- `installation_policy_before`: Installation policy before the update.
- `installation_policy`: Installation policy after the update.
- `installed_by_default_role_ids_before`: Role identifiers for which the plugin was installed by default before the update.
- `installed_by_default_role_ids`: Role identifiers for which the plugin is installed by default after the update.

**CUSTOM_GPT_SET_ALLOWED_ACTION_DOMAINS** — Updated the third-party action domain allowlist for a GPT.
- `domains`: List of allowed domains; may be `null` to clear the list.

**CUSTOM_GPT_DELETE** — Removal of a GPT from the workspace catalog.
- `id`: GPT identifier that was deleted.

**CUSTOM_GPT_CHANGE_OWNER** — Transfer of GPT ownership.
- `id`: GPT identifier being reassigned.
- `new_owner_email`: Email of the new owner.

**CUSTOM_GPT_CHANGE_VISIBILITY** — Updated GPT sharing audience.
- `id`: GPT identifier whose sharing state changed.
- `shared_to`: Array of `GizmoSharingParam` objects describing each recipient segment. Each element includes a `type` such as `private`, `email`, `user`, `group`, `workspace`, `workspace_link`, `link`, or `marketplace` and any supporting identifiers (e.g., `user_email`, `user_id`, `group_id`).

**CUSTOM_GPT_ALLOW_THIRD_PARTY** — Workspace-level toggle of third-party GPT permissions.
- `value`: String payload describing the permission state for the third-party GPT.

**CUSTOM_GPT_APPROVE_THIRD_PARTY_FOR_WORKSPACE** — Approval of a third-party GPT for workspace use.
- `third_party_gizmo_id`: Identifier of the approved GPT.

**CUSTOM_GPT_REMOVE_THIRD_PARTY_FOR_WORKSPACE** — Removal of a third-party GPT approval.
- `third_party_gizmo_id`: Identifier of the GPT whose approval was revoked.

**DOMAIN_CREATE** — Addition of an allowed email or URL domain.
- `hostname`: Domain hostname that was added.
- `domain_id`: Identifier of the managed domain entry.

**DOMAIN_DELETE** — Removal of an allowed domain.
- `domain_id`: Identifier of the domain record that was deleted.

**DOMAIN_CHECK** — Triggered verification check for a domain.
- `domain_id`: Identifier of the domain being checked.

**GROUP_CREATE** — Creation of a user group.
- `group_id`: Identifier of the new group.
- `name`: Group name.

**GROUP_EDIT** — Updated group metadata or membership.
- `group_id`: Identifier of the group that changed.
- `new_name`: New group name, when provided.
- `added_user_id`: Auth user ID that was added, when applicable.

**GROUP_ADD_USERS** — Bulk addition of users to a group via email.
- `group_id`: Identifier of the group.
- `email_addresses`: List of user emails that were added.

**GROUP_REMOVE_USER** — Removal of a user from a group.
- `group_id`: Identifier of the group.
- `removed_user_id`: Auth user ID that was removed.

**GROUP_DELETE** — Deletion of a group.
- `group_id`: Identifier of the group that was deleted.

**INVITE_USERS** — Workspace invitations were issued.
- `email_addresses`: List of invitee emails.
- `role`: Role assigned to the invitees.

**INVITE_DELETE** — An outstanding invitation was revoked.
- `email_address`: Email whose invite was deleted.

**INVITE_USER_REQUEST** — Logged an inbound request to join the workspace.
- `email_address`: Email of the requester.

**INVITE_ACCEPT_ALL** — Admin approved all outstanding join requests.
- `total_requested`: Count of requests that were approved.

**INVITE_SET_AUTO_ACCEPT_JOIN_REQUESTS** — Updated auto-accept setting for join requests.
- `value`: Boolean indicating whether requests are auto-approved.

**INVITE_SET_ALLOW_EXTERNAL_DOMAINS** — Toggled whether external domains can request access.
- `value`: Boolean describing the new policy state.

**SAML_CREATE_CONNECTION** — Configured a new SAML connection.
- `sign_in_endpoint`: SAML sign-in endpoint URL for the connection.

**SCIM_SET_EMAIL_INVITES_ENABLED** — Updated SCIM email invite behavior.
- `sign_in_endpoint`: Identifier of the SCIM connection whose email invite policy changed.

**SUBSCRIPTION_SET_OVERAGE_LIMIT** — Modified the credit overage allowance.
- `overage_limit_credits`: Integer credit limit or the string `"unlimited"`.

**SUBSCRIPTION_SET_USAGE_ALERTS** — Adjusted usage alerting thresholds.
- `alert_recipients`: List of recipients (each `AlertRecipient` includes `type="email"` and an email `value`).
- `alert_thresholds`: List of thresholds (each `AlertThreshold` includes `type="absolute"` and the credit `credits`).

**USER_DELETE** — Admin deleted a user account.
- `deleted_user_id`: Auth user ID that was deleted.

**USER_ROLE_UPDATED** — Admin changed a user's workspace role.
- `user_id`: Auth user ID whose role changed.
- `new_role`: Role value that the user was updated to (e.g., `"account-admin"`).

**USER_LOGGED_OUT_BY_ADMIN** — Admin forced a logout for a user.
- `logged_out_user_id`: Auth user ID that was logged out.

**WORKSPACE_TOGGLE_FEATURE** — Enabled or disabled a workspace feature flag.
- `feature`: Feature identifier that toggled.
- `value`: Boolean describing the resulting state.
- `app_id`: App identifier when the toggle applies to a specific app.
- `source_surface`: Optional admin surface that initiated the toggle; either `admin_apps` or `admin_plugins`.
- `context_plugin_id`: Optional plugin identifier whose UI initiated the toggle.
- `affected_connector_ids`: Connector identifiers whose workspace permissions were affected.
- `changed_fields`: Workspace-permission fields changed by the toggle.
- `changed_fields_by_connector`: Mapping from connector identifier to fields changed for that connector.
- `previous_workspace_permissions_by_connector`: Mapping from connector identifier to its workspace-permission snapshot before the toggle.
- `new_workspace_permissions_by_connector`: Mapping from connector identifier to its workspace-permission snapshot after the toggle.

**WORKSPACE_SET_SHARING_PERMISSION** — Updated workspace-level sharing permissions (legacy RBAC toggle).
- `feature`: Sharing feature that changed.
- `value`: Boolean describing whether the feature is enabled.

**WORKSPACE_SET_SYSTEM_INSTRUCTION** — Changed the default workspace system instructions supplied to ChatGPT.
- `system_instruction`: The full system prompt now applied to users.

**WORKSPACE_SET_POLICY** — Updated workspace policy text.
- `workspace_policy`: Policy document or identifier that now applies.

**WORKSPACE_SET_FEDRAMP_BANNER** — Updated the FedRAMP workspace banner configuration.
- `enabled`: Boolean describing whether the banner is enabled.
- `classification`: Classification string shown in the banner header.
- `markdown`: Markdown body shown in the banner content.

**WORKSPACE_SET_AUTO_PROVISION** — Toggled automatic user provisioning.
- `value`: Boolean describing whether auto-provision is enabled.

**WORKSPACE_SET_COMPLIANCE_API_IP_ALLOWLIST** — Replaced the IP allowlist for Compliance API consumption.
- `allowed_ips`: Array of CIDR strings that now form the allowlist.

**WORKSPACE_SET_IP_ALLOWLIST** — Updated the general workspace IP allowlist.
- `allowed_ips`: Array of CIDR strings now allowed to access the workspace.

**WORKSPACE_SET_IS_DISCOVERABLE** — Changed workspace discoverability settings.
- `value`: Boolean describing whether the workspace is discoverable.
- `public_display_name`: Optional display name shown externally.
- `use_workspace_name_for_discovery`: Boolean indicating if the workspace name is reused for discovery.

### User actions
**PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN_CREATE** — User created a v2 personal access token.
- `credential_id`: Identifier of the personal access token credential.
- `credential_type`: Credential type; currently `personal_access_token`.
- `credential_name`: User-provided name of the credential.
- `owner_user_id`: Auth user ID of the credential owner.
- `workspace_id`: Workspace in which the credential was issued.
- `expires_at`: Credential expiration time in epoch seconds, or `null` when it does not expire.
- `scopes`: Sorted, deduplicated list of product-access scopes stored on the credential.

**PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN_REVOKE** — User revoked their own v2 personal access token.
- `credential_id`: Identifier of the personal access token credential.
- `credential_type`: Credential type; currently `personal_access_token`.
- `credential_name`: User-provided name of the credential.
- `owner_user_id`: Auth user ID of the credential owner.
- `workspace_id`: Workspace in which the credential was issued.
- `expires_at`: Credential expiration time in epoch seconds, or `null` when it does not expire.
- `scopes`: Sorted, deduplicated list of product-access scopes stored on the credential.
- `revoked_at`: Persisted revocation time in epoch seconds, or `null` for a legacy deleted credential without a revocation timestamp.
- `state_changed`: Whether this successful request performed the initial revoke transition.

**SESSION_LOGOUT_ALL** — User manually invalidated all active sessions. `action_data` is empty for this action.

**SESSION_REVOKE** — User revoked a single active session from Session Manager, remotely ending that session.
- `session_id`: Unified session ID requested for revocation.
- `revoked_unified_sessions`: Unified session IDs revoked by the request.

**CONVERSATION_DELETE** — User deleted a conversation.
- `conversation_id`: Identifier of the conversation that was removed.

**CONVERSATION_SHARE** — User created a shared conversation link.
- `conversation_id`: Identifier of the underlying conversation that was shared.
- `shared_conversation_id`: Identifier of the new shared conversation that was created.
- `already_exists`: True if a shared conversation already existed and so was returned directly.

**CONVERSATION_VIEW_OF_SHARED** — User viewed a shared conversation link.
- `shared_conversation_id`: Identifier of the shared conversation link that was viewed.
- `conversation_id`: Identifier of the underlying conversation that was viewed through the shared link.

**CUSTOM_GPT_UPDATE_SHARING** — User updated GPT sharing audience.
- `id`: GPT identifier whose sharing state changed.
- `shared_to`: Array of recipient records describing each sharing audience segment. Each element includes `recipient_type` (such as `private`, `email`, `user`, `group`, `workspace`, `workspace_link`, `link`, or `marketplace`), optional recipient identifiers such as `user_email`, `user_id`, or `group_id`, and `capabilities`.

**PROJECT_UPDATE_SHARING** — User updated project sharing audience.
- `id`: Project identifier whose sharing state changed.
- `shared_to`: Optional array of recipient records describing the final sharing audience after the request.
- `requested_access_updates`: Optional array of recipient records that the request asked to add or update. For visibility-level records such as `private`, `link`, or `workspace_link`, this is the requested visibility replacement.
- `requested_access_removals`: Optional array of recipient records that the request asked to remove. Visibility-level records are changed through `requested_access_updates`, not removals.

**SITE_UPDATE_ACCESS_POLICY** — User successfully updated a Site access policy, either directly or as part of a Site ownership transfer.
- `project_id`: Identifier of the Site whose access policy changed.
- `revision`: Access policy revision after the change.
- `access_mode_before`: Access mode before the change. One of `admins_only`, `workspace_all`, `custom`, or `public`.
- `access_mode`: Access mode after the change. One of `admins_only`, `workspace_all`, `custom`, or `public`.
- `added_user_ids`: Auth user IDs (`user-*`) granted direct access by the change.
- `removed_user_ids`: Auth user IDs (`user-*`) whose direct access was removed by the change.
- `allowed_workspace_group_ids_before`: Complete set of workspace group IDs with access before the change.
- `allowed_workspace_group_ids`: Complete set of workspace group IDs with access after the change.
- `allowed_tenant_group_ids_before`: Complete set of tenant group IDs with access before the change. Tenant groups can span workspaces in the tenant associated with the Site's workspace.
- `allowed_tenant_group_ids`: Complete set of tenant group IDs with access after the change. Tenant groups can span workspaces in the tenant associated with the Site's workspace.
- `changed_fields`: Access policy components that changed. Possible values are `access_mode`, `direct_users`, `workspace_groups`, and `tenant_groups`.
- `client_id`: Normalized Codex client identifier for the surface that initiated the change.
- `triggering_action`: Sites action that caused the policy update. One of `update_site_access` or `transfer_site_ownership`.

**CONVERSATION_MESSAGE_RATING** — User submitted a rating associated with a message in a conversation.
- `conversation_id`: Identifier of the conversation containing the rated message context.
- `message_id`: Identifier of the message associated with the rating.
- `rating`: Rating the user submitted. One of `"thumbs_up"` or `"thumbs_down"`.

**CONVERSATION_MESSAGE_RATING_DELETE** — User removed a message rating in a conversation.
- `conversation_id`: Identifier of the conversation containing the rated message.
- `message_id`: Identifier of the message whose rating was removed.

**FILE_DOWNLOAD** — User requested a file download.
- `file_id`: Identifier of the file requested for download, when available.
- `file_name`: Name of the file requested for download, when available.
- `mime_type`: MIME type of the file requested for download, when available.

**INVITE_ACCEPT** — Recorded that a user accepted an invitation to join the workspace.
- `email_address`: Email of the new member.

**SKILL_CREATE** — User created a skill.
- `skill_id`: Identifier of the skill that was created.
- `skill_name`: Name of the skill at creation time.

**SKILL_UPDATE** — User updated a skill.
- `skill_id`: Identifier of the skill that was updated.
- `skill_name`: Name of the skill after the update.

**SKILL_DELETE** — User deleted a skill.
- `skill_id`: Identifier of the skill that was deleted.
- `skill_name`: Name of the skill that was deleted.


**SKILL_SHARE** — User shared a skill.
- `skill_id`: Identifier of the skill that was shared.
- `skill_name`: Name of the skill that was shared.
- `principal_type`: Principal type for the share target.
- `principal_id`: Principal identifier for the share target.
- `role`: Role granted to the share target.
- `previous_role`: Previous role for the share target (nullable).

**SKILL_WORKSPACE_ACCESS** — User changed workspace access state for a skill.
- `skill_id`: Identifier of the skill whose workspace access was changed.
- `skill_name`: Name of the skill whose workspace access was changed.
- `workspace_id`: Workspace identifier for which access was changed.
- `workspace_access_state`: New workspace access state. One of `restricted`, `discoverable`, or `enabled`.

**SKILL_UNSHARE** — User unshared a skill.
- `skill_id`: Identifier of the skill that was unshared.
- `skill_name`: Name of the skill that was unshared.
- `principal_type`: Principal type for the share target.
- `principal_id`: Principal identifier for the share target.
- `role`: Role removed from the share target.

**WORKSPACE_POLICY_ACKNOWLEDGEMENT** — User acknowledge the workspace policy.

### API key actions
These actions are emitted when public workspace API requests use API key authentication (`actor.type = "API_KEY"`). Compliance API endpoint requests and Admin API endpoint requests use the actions documented in this section.
`action_privilege` is `ADMIN` for all actions in this section.

**LIST_CODE_ENVIRONMENTS** — Listed Codex environments in a workspace.
- `limit`: Requested page size.
- `after`: Pagination cursor.

**LIST_CODEX_TASKS** — Listed Codex tasks in a workspace.

**GET_CODEX_TASK** — Retrieved a specific Codex task.
- `task_id`: Task identifier.

**GET_CODE_ENVIRONMENT** — Retrieved a specific Codex environment.
- `codex_environment_id`: Environment identifier.

**LIST_PLUGINS** — Listed live workspace-scoped plugins in a workspace.
- `cursor`: Pagination cursor.
- `limit`: Requested page size.

**GET_PLUGIN** — Retrieved a specific live workspace-scoped plugin.
- `plugin_id`: Plugin identifier.

**LIST_REMOTE_CONTROL_ENVIRONMENTS** — Listed Codex remote-control environments for a workspace user.
- `user_id`: User identifier.
- `cursor`: Pagination cursor.
- `limit`: Requested page size.

**GET_REMOTE_CONTROL_ENVIRONMENT** — Retrieved a specific Codex remote-control environment for a workspace user.
- `user_id`: User identifier.
- `environment_id`: Remote-control environment identifier.

**LIST_REMOTE_CONTROL_THREADS** — Listed Codex remote-control threads for a workspace user environment.
- `user_id`: User identifier.
- `environment_id`: Remote-control environment identifier.
- `cursor`: Pagination cursor.
- `limit`: Requested page size.

**GET_REMOTE_CONTROL_THREAD** — Retrieved a specific Codex remote-control thread for a workspace user environment.
- `user_id`: User identifier.
- `environment_id`: Remote-control environment identifier.
- `remote_thread_id`: Remote-control thread identifier.

**LIST_REMOTE_CONTROL_CLIENTS** — Listed Codex remote-control clients for a workspace user.
- `user_id`: User identifier.
- `cursor`: Pagination cursor.
- `limit`: Requested page size.

**GET_REMOTE_CONTROL_CLIENT** — Retrieved a specific Codex remote-control client for a workspace user.
- `user_id`: User identifier.
- `client_id`: Remote-control client identifier.

**LIST_WORKSPACE_GPTS** — Listed GPTs in a workspace.
- `after`: Pagination cursor.
- `limit`: Requested page size.
- `file_format`: File output mode (`url` or `id`).

**LIST_WORKSPACE_AGENTS** — Listed Workspace Agents in a workspace.
- `owner_id`: Optional owner user ID filter.
- `cursor`: Pagination cursor.
- `limit`: Requested page size.

**GET_WORKSPACE_AGENT** — Retrieved Workspace Agent metadata and definition.
- `agent_id`: Workspace Agent identifier.

**GET_GPT_INFO** — Retrieved GPT metadata.
- `gpt_id`: GPT identifier.
- `file_format`: File output mode (`url` or `id`).

**LIST_WORKSPACE_GPT_USERS** — Listed GPT shared users.
- `gpt_id`: GPT identifier.
- `after`: Pagination cursor.
- `limit`: Requested page size.

**LIST_WORKSPACE_GPT_CONFIGS** — Listed GPT configurations.
- `gpt_id`: GPT identifier.

tags.name: Codex
tags.description:
This section describes the Codex compliance log files and their format as available through the OpenAI Compliance Logs Platform.

Each Codex log entry corresponds to a Codex client action, such as prompt/response activity, tool calls, app MCP calls, plugin lifecycle changes, environment lifecycle changes, or Sites lifecycle changes.

`event_type` = `CODEX_LOG`
Fine-grained API key scope: `chatgpt.enterprise.compliance_logs_platform.codex_log.read`.
API keys with `chatgpt.enterprise.compliance_logs_platform.read` or the legacy
`chatgpt.enterprise.compliance_export.read` scope can also read Codex.

### Schema
Each event conforms to the shared Logs Platform envelope described above with these additional top-level fields:
- `type`: Always `CODEX_LOG`.
- `event_type`: Codex sub-event type. One of:
  - `ENVIRONMENT_CREATED`
  - `ENVIRONMENT_UPDATED`
  - `ENVIRONMENT_DELETED`
  - `WORKSPACE_UPDATED`
  - `PROMPT_SENT`
  - `PROMPT_RESPONSE_RECEIVED`
  - `TOOL_CALL_SUGGESTED`
  - `TOOL_CALL_COMPLETED`
  - `TOOL_CALL_FAILED`
  - `ACCESS_TOKEN_CREATED`
  - `ACCESS_TOKEN_REVOKED`
  - `APP_MCP_CALL`
  - `APP_MCP_RESULT`
  - `APP_MCP_ELICITATION`
  - `PLUGIN_CREATED`
  - `PLUGIN_DELETED`
  - `PLUGIN_INSTALLED`
  - `PLUGIN_UNINSTALLED`
  - `SITE_PROJECT_CREATED`
  - `SITE_PROJECT_DELETED`
  - `SITE_VERSION_CREATED`
  - `SITE_DEPLOYMENT_STARTED`
  - `SITE_DEPLOYMENT_COMPLETED`
- `client_id`: Normalized Codex client identifier (e.g., `CODEX_CLI`, `CODEX_WEB`, `CODEX_DESKTOP_APP`, `CODEX_IDE_VSCODE`, `CODEX_GITHUB_ACTION`, `CODEX_SDK_TS`, `CODEX_SERVICE_EXEC`, `CODEX_UNKNOWN_DEFAULT`).
- `workspace_id`: Workspace identifier.
- `event_details`: Object shaped according to `event_type` (see below).

#### event_details by `event_type`
- `ENVIRONMENT_CREATED`
  - `detail_type`: Always `ENVIRONMENT_CREATED`.
  - `environment_id`: Identifier for the environment.
  - `environment_fields`: Sanitized, non-sensitive environment snapshot (label, description, repos, cache/agent settings, permissions, env_var_keys, etc.).
- `ENVIRONMENT_UPDATED`
  - `detail_type`: Always `ENVIRONMENT_UPDATED`.
  - `environment_id`: Identifier for the environment.
  - `environment_fields`: Sanitized, non-sensitive environment fields that were provided/updated (same keys as created).
- `ENVIRONMENT_DELETED`
  - `detail_type`: Always `ENVIRONMENT_DELETED`.
  - `environment_id`: Identifier for the environment.
- `WORKSPACE_UPDATED`
  - `detail_type`: Always `WORKSPACE_UPDATED`.
  - `previous_settings`: Optional sanitized settings snapshot before the change.
  - `current_settings`: Optional sanitized settings snapshot after the change.
- `PROMPT_SENT`
  - `detail_type`: Always `PROMPT_SENT`.
  - `session_id`: Session identifier used to correlate prompts/responses.
  - `prompt_text`: Extracted user prompt text (may be empty for non-text inputs).
  - `turn_id`: Optional turn identifier.
  - `call_id`: Optional request/call identifier.
  - `model`: Optional model name.
  - `environment_id`: Optional identifier for the environment in use.
- `PROMPT_RESPONSE_RECEIVED`
  - `detail_type`: Always `PROMPT_RESPONSE_RECEIVED`.
  - `session_id`: Session identifier used to correlate prompts/responses.
  - `response_text`: Model response text (may be empty for non-text outputs).
  - `status`: Response status string.
  - `turn_id`: Optional turn identifier.
  - `call_id`: Optional request/call identifier.
  - `model`: Model name.
  - `service_tier`: Optional service tier used for the response.
  - `reasoning_effort`: Optional resolved reasoning effort used for the response.
  - `token_usage`: Object with `input_tokens`, `output_tokens`, `cached_input_tokens`, `reasoning_output_tokens`.
  - `environment_id`: Optional identifier for the environment in use.
- `TOOL_CALL_SUGGESTED`, `TOOL_CALL_COMPLETED`, `TOOL_CALL_FAILED`
  - `detail_type`: Always matches the top-level tool-call `event_type`.
  - `session_id`: Session identifier used to correlate tool calls with prompts/responses.
  - `tool_name`: Tool name.
  - `tool_type`: Tool type/category.
  - `tool_input`: Serialized tool input.
  - `turn_id`: Optional turn identifier.
  - `call_id`: Optional request/call identifier.
  - `tool_call_id`: Optional tool-call identifier.
  - `status`: Optional tool-call status.
  - `model`: Optional model name.
  - `environment_id`: Optional identifier for the environment in use.
- `ACCESS_TOKEN_CREATED`, `ACCESS_TOKEN_REVOKED`
  - `detail_type`: Always matches the top-level access-token `event_type`.
  - `access_token_id`: Identifier for the Codex access token.
  - `access_token_name`: Human-readable token name.
  - `created_by_user_id`: User ID of the token creator.
  - `expires_at`: Optional expiration timestamp.
- `APP_MCP_CALL`
  - `detail_type`: Always `APP_MCP_CALL`.
  - `call_id`: Optional call identifier.
  - `name`: MCP tool name.
  - `arguments`: MCP call arguments.
  - `tool_meta`: Optional tool metadata such as connector or resource identifiers.
- `APP_MCP_RESULT`
  - `detail_type`: Always `APP_MCP_RESULT`.
  - `call_id`: Optional call identifier.
  - `name`: MCP tool name.
  - `status`: Result status string.
  - `error_code`: Optional error code.
  - `error_message`: Optional error message.
  - `result_preview`: Optional truncated result preview.
- `APP_MCP_ELICITATION`
  - `detail_type`: Always `APP_MCP_ELICITATION`.
  - `call_id`: Optional call identifier.
  - `name`: MCP tool name.
  - `elicitation_type`: Elicitation type.
  - `phase`: Elicitation phase.
  - `decision`: Optional user decision.
  - `url`: Optional related URL.
- `PLUGIN_CREATED`, `PLUGIN_DELETED`, `PLUGIN_INSTALLED`, `PLUGIN_UNINSTALLED`
  - `detail_type`: Always matches the top-level plugin lifecycle `event_type`.
  - `plugin_id`: Stable plugin identity.
  - `plugin_release_id`: Exact plugin release/artifact associated with the lifecycle action.
  - `plugin_version`: Plugin version string.
  - `plugin_name`: Machine-readable plugin name.
  - `plugin_display_name`: Human-readable plugin display name.
  - `marketplace_name`: Optional catalog/provenance name such as `openai-curated`.
  - `plugin_scope`: Plugin definition scope. `GLOBAL` is a globally available server-backed plugin, `WORKSPACE` is owned by a workspace, and `USER` is owned by a single account user.
  - `plugin_creator_account_user_id`: Optional creator/importer account-user ID, usually present for workspace and user plugins.
- `SITE_PROJECT_CREATED`
  - `detail_type`: Always `SITE_PROJECT_CREATED`.
  - `project_id`: Stable identifier of the Site project.
  - `slug`: Site slug at creation time.
- `SITE_PROJECT_DELETED`
  - `detail_type`: Always `SITE_PROJECT_DELETED`.
  - `project_id`: Stable identifier of the Site project.
  - `slug`: Site slug at deletion time.
- `SITE_VERSION_CREATED`
  - `detail_type`: Always `SITE_VERSION_CREATED`.
  - `project_id`: Identifier of the Site project.
  - `version_id`: Identifier of the created Site version.
  - `version_number`: Sequential version number within the Site project.
- `SITE_DEPLOYMENT_STARTED`
  - `detail_type`: Always `SITE_DEPLOYMENT_STARTED`.
  - `project_id`: Identifier of the Site project.
  - `version_id`: Identifier of the Site version being deployed.
  - `deployment_id`: Identifier of the Site deployment.
  - `environment_revision`: Environment configuration revision used by the deployment.
- `SITE_DEPLOYMENT_COMPLETED`
  - `detail_type`: Always `SITE_DEPLOYMENT_COMPLETED`.
  - `project_id`: Identifier of the Site project.
  - `version_id`: Identifier of the deployed Site version.
  - `deployment_id`: Identifier of the Site deployment.
  - `status`: Deployment outcome. One of `success` or `failed`.
  - `environment_revision`: Environment configuration revision used by the deployment.
  - `site_url`: URL of the deployed Site when the deployment succeeded; otherwise `null` or omitted.

### Example records
**Prompt sent**
```json
{
  "event_id": "c97ee69d-41a6-4587-91ee-1ccb1afabe2e",
  "type": "CODEX_LOG",
  "timestamp": "2025-09-25T23:43:58.762392Z",
  "principal": {
    "id": "be545252-ad04-4cfa-9ca5-deca58416151",
    "type": "CHATGPT_WORKSPACE"
  },
  "actor": {
    "type": "ACCOUNT_USER",
    "user_id": "user-TUvqhBX7HbQPRgHyEBt5WRcI",
    "user_email": "user@example.org"
  },
  "event_type": "PROMPT_SENT",
  "client_id": "CODEX_CLI",
  "workspace_id": "be545252-ad04-4cfa-9ca5-deca58416151",
  "event_details": {
    "detail_type": "PROMPT_SENT",
    "session_id": "session-123",
    "prompt_text": "Summarize the latest changes in the repo.",
    "model": "gpt-5.1-codex-max",

```

This section describes the Codex Security compliance log files and their format as available through the OpenAI Compliance Logs Platform.

Each Codex Security log entry corresponds to a security or remediation action in Codex Security.

`event_type` = `CODEX_SECURITY_LOG`
Fine-grained API key scope: `chatgpt.enterprise.compliance_logs_platform.codex_security_log.read`.
API keys with `chatgpt.enterprise.compliance_logs_platform.read` or the legacy
`chatgpt.enterprise.compliance_export.read` scope can also read Codex Security.

### Schema
Each event conforms to the shared Logs Platform envelope described above with these additional top-level fields:
- `type`: Always `CODEX_SECURITY_LOG`.
- `event_type`: Codex Security sub-event type. Currently one of:
  - `SCAN_CONFIGURATION_CREATED`
  - `SCAN_CONFIGURATION_UPDATED`
  - `SCAN_FINDING_UPDATED`
  - `PROPOSED_PATCH_PR_CREATED`
- `client_id`: Normalized client identifier derived from the request originator (for example, `CODEX_WEB`).
- `workspace_id`: Workspace identifier.
- `event_details`: Object shaped according to `event_type` (see below).

#### event_details by `event_type`
- `SCAN_CONFIGURATION_CREATED`
  - `detail_type`: Always `SCAN_CONFIGURATION_CREATED`.
  - `scan_configuration_id`: Product-facing scan configuration identifier.
  - `scan_configuration_fields`: Sanitized scan configuration snapshot. Includes non-sensitive fields such as `scan_type`, `owner_id`, `workspace_id`, `repo_id`, `repo_url`, `environment_id`, `state`, `lookback_days`, and summarized notification rule delta counts (`notification_rules_created_count`, `notification_rules_updated_count`, `notification_rules_deleted_count`).
- `SCAN_CONFIGURATION_UPDATED`
  - `detail_type`: Always `SCAN_CONFIGURATION_UPDATED`.
  - `scan_configuration_id`: Product-facing scan configuration identifier.
  - `updated_fields`: The subset of scan configuration fields that changed. Includes `environment_id`, `state`, `owner_id`, `lookback_days`, sanitized `project_overview` metadata (`project_overview_updated`, `project_overview_length`), and summarized notification rule delta counts (`notification_rules_created_count`, `notification_rules_updated_count`, `notification_rules_deleted_count`).
  - `scan_configuration_fields`: Sanitized post-update scan configuration snapshot.
- `SCAN_FINDING_UPDATED`
  - `detail_type`: Always `SCAN_FINDING_UPDATED`.
  - `finding_id`: Scan finding identifier.
  - `updated_fields`: The subset of finding fields that changed. Includes `status`, `assignee_user_email`, `criticality`, `resolution_reason`, `resolution_reason_updated`, `criticality_reason`, and `criticality_reason_updated`.
- `PROPOSED_PATCH_PR_CREATED`
  - `detail_type`: Always `PROPOSED_PATCH_PR_CREATED`.
  - `finding_id`: Scan finding identifier.
  - `pr_url`: Pull request URL when available. This may be `null` if pull request metadata refresh is unavailable after creation.

tags.name: Workspace Agents
tags.description:
This section describes the Workspace Agents compliance log files and their format as available through the OpenAI Compliance Logs Platform.

Each Workspace Agents log entry corresponds to agent lifecycle activity, runtime usage, trigger changes, or connector OAuth resolution performed while using an agent.

`event_type` = `CUSTOM_AGENTS_LOG`
Fine-grained API key scope: `chatgpt.enterprise.compliance_logs_platform.custom_agents_log.read`.
API keys with `chatgpt.enterprise.compliance_logs_platform.read` or the legacy
`chatgpt.enterprise.compliance_export.read` scope can also read Workspace Agents.

### Schema
Each event conforms to the shared Logs Platform envelope described above with these additional top-level fields:
- `type`: Always `CUSTOM_AGENTS_LOG`.
- `event_type`: Workspace Agents sub-event type. One of:
  - `AGENT_CREATED`
  - `AGENT_DELETED`
  - `AGENT_PUBLISHED`
  - `AGENT_RUN_COMPLETED`
  - `AGENT_RUN_CREATED`
  - `AGENT_RUN_FAILED`
  - `AGENT_RUN_MESSAGE`
  - `AGENT_UPDATED`
  - `CONNECTOR_CALL_COMPLETED`
  - `CONNECTOR_CALL_REQUESTED`
  - `CONNECTOR_OAUTH_RESOLVED`
  - `MEMORY_DELETE`
  - `MEMORY_READ`
  - `MEMORY_WRITE`
  - `SKILL_USED`
  - `TRIGGER_CREATED`
  - `TRIGGER_DELETED`
  - `TRIGGER_UPDATED`
- `client_id`: Normalized Workspace Agents client identifier. One of `AGENT_BUILDER_WEB`, `CHATGPT_WEB`, `ENTERPRISE_COMPLIANCE_API`, `FIRST_PARTY_ECOSYSTEM`, or `CUSTOM_AGENTS_UNKNOWN`.
- `workspace_id`: Workspace identifier.
- `event_details`: Object shaped according to `event_type` (see below).

#### event_details by `event_type`
- `AGENT_CREATED`
  - `detail_type`: Always `AGENT_CREATED`.
  - `agent_id`: Identifier for the agent.
  - `version_id`: Identifier for the saved version.
  - `agent_fields`: Sanitized agent snapshot including model, name, prompt, description, tagline, category, starter prompts, file_tree_id, skills, and tool metadata.
- `AGENT_DELETED`
  - `detail_type`: Always `AGENT_DELETED`.
  - `agent_id`: Identifier for the agent.
  - `version_id`: Optional identifier for the previously published version.
  - `delete_reason`: Reason label for the delete action.
  - `agent_fields`: Sanitized agent snapshot captured immediately before the delete completed.
  - `trigger_count`: Count of triggers linked to the agent at delete time.
  - `had_published_version`: Whether the agent had a published version at the time of deletion.
- `AGENT_PUBLISHED`
  - `detail_type`: Always `AGENT_PUBLISHED`.
  - `agent_id`: Identifier for the agent.
  - `version_id`: Identifier for the published version.
  - `publish_type`: Publication mode.
  - `changes_count`: Optional count of included changes.
  - `release_name`: Optional release title.
  - `release_description`: Optional release description.
  - `agent_fields`: Sanitized agent snapshot including the published tool and connector configuration.
- `AGENT_RUN_COMPLETED`
  - `detail_type`: Always `AGENT_RUN_COMPLETED`.
  - `agent_id`: Identifier for the agent.
  - `version_id`: Identifier for the runtime version.
  - `run_id`: Stable runtime identifier used to correlate later activity for the same run.
  - Emitted only for successful terminal runs.
- `AGENT_RUN_CREATED`
  - `detail_type`: Always `AGENT_RUN_CREATED`.
  - `agent_id`: Identifier for the agent.
  - `version_id`: Identifier for the runtime version.
  - `run_id`: Stable runtime identifier used to correlate later activity for the same run.
  - `conversation_id`: Optional conversation identifier for ChatGPT custom-agent invocations.
  - `invoker`: Structured invoker identity object.
    - `type`: Invoker type. Current exhaustive values:
      - `chatgpt`
      - `api_trigger`
      - `webhook_trigger`
      - `schedule_trigger`
    - `initiator`: Structured initiator identity object.
      - `kind`: Initiator kind. Current exhaustive values:
        - `account_user`
        - `trigger_api`
        - `trigger_generic`
        - `trigger_schedule`
        - `trigger_webhook`
      - `id`: Initiator identifier. For `trigger_api`, this is the stable API trigger identifier rather than the request identifier.
      - `display_name`: Optional initiator display name.
      - `auth_user_id`: Optional auth user identifier when available.
    - `user_message_text`: Optional end-user message text that started a ChatGPT custom-agent run.
    - `is_shared_invocation`: Optional boolean for ChatGPT shared-agent invocations.
    - `connector_id`: Optional connector identifier for webhook trigger invocations.
    - `webhook_name`: Optional webhook name for webhook trigger invocations.
    - `schedule_id`: Optional schedule identifier for scheduled trigger invocations.
    - API trigger invocations use `type: api_trigger` and do not populate `connector_id`, `webhook_name`, or `schedule_id`.
- `AGENT_RUN_FAILED`
  - `detail_type`: Always `AGENT_RUN_FAILED`.
  - `agent_id`: Identifier for the agent.
  - `version_id`: Identifier for the runtime version.
  - `run_id`: Stable runtime identifier used to correlate later activity for the same run.
  - `failure_message`: Terminal failure string for incident triage. When a runtime message is available it is prefixed with the terminal fiber status; otherwise it falls back to the terminal fiber status alone.
- `AGENT_RUN_MESSAGE`
  - `detail_type`: Always `AGENT_RUN_MESSAGE`.
  - `agent_id`: Identifier for the agent.
  - `version_id`: Identifier for the runtime version.
  - `run_id`: Stable runtime identifier used to correlate later activity for the same run.
  - `message_id`: Runtime message identifier.
  - `text`: Optional extracted displayable agent-authored message text.
  - `phase`: Optional agent message phase. One of `commentary` or `final_answer` when present.
  - This event currently exports agent messages only; end-user messages are not included.
- `AGENT_UPDATED`
  - `detail_type`: Always `AGENT_UPDATED`.
  - `agent_id`: Identifier for the agent.
  - `version_id`: Identifier for the saved version.
  - `save_source`: Optional save source label.
  - `agent_fields`: Sanitized agent snapshot including the current tool and connector configuration.
- `CONNECTOR_CALL_COMPLETED`
  - `detail_type`: Always `CONNECTOR_CALL_COMPLETED`.
  - `agent_id`: Identifier for the agent.
  - `version_id`: Identifier for the runtime version.
  - `run_id`: Stable runtime identifier used to correlate later activity for the same run.
  - `tool_call_id`: Tool call identifier for the connector usage.
  - `connector_id`: Connector identifier.
  - `connector_name`: Connector display name.
  - `action_name`: Connector action name.
  - `link_id`: Optional connector link identifier when the connector tool uses a linked auth variant.
  - `status`: Normalized connector call result. One of `success` or `failed`.
- `CONNECTOR_CALL_REQUESTED`
  - `detail_type`: Always `CONNECTOR_CALL_REQUESTED`.
  - `agent_id`: Identifier for the agent.
  - `version_id`: Identifier for the runtime version.
  - `run_id`: Stable runtime identifier used to correlate later activity for the same run.
  - `tool_call_id`: Tool call identifier for the connector usage.
  - `connector_id`: Connector identifier.
  - `connector_name`: Connector display name.
  - `action_name`: Connector action name.
  - `link_id`: Optional connector link identifier when the connector tool uses a linked auth variant.
  - `requires_elicitation`: Optional boolean indicating whether the agent determined the tool call needs elicitation before execution.
  - `elicitation_type`: Optional elicitation mode when present. One of `approval` or `end_user_auth`.
- `CONNECTOR_OAUTH_RESOLVED`
  - `detail_type`: Always `CONNECTOR_OAUTH_RESOLVED`.
  - `agent_id`: Identifier for the agent.
  - `version_id`: Identifier for the runtime version.
  - `conversation_id`: Optional conversation identifier.
  - `run_id`: Runtime run identifier.
  - `interaction_id`: Interaction identifier.
  - `tool_call_id`: Tool call identifier.
  - `connector_id`: Optional connector identifier resolved from runtime context.
  - `link_id`: Connector link identifier.
- `MEMORY_DELETE`
  - `detail_type`: Always `MEMORY_DELETE`.
  - `agent_id`: Identifier for the agent.
  - `version_id`: Identifier for the runtime version.
  - `run_id`: Stable runtime identifier used to correlate later activity for the same run.
  - `memory_path`: Memory file path relative to the agent Memory root.
  - `access_method`: Always `delete`.
- `MEMORY_READ`
  - `detail_type`: Always `MEMORY_READ`.
  - `agent_id`: Identifier for the agent.
  - `version_id`: Identifier for the runtime version.
  - `run_id`: Stable runtime identifier used to correlate later activity for the same run.
  - `memory_path`: Memory file or directory path relative to the agent Memory root.
  - `access_method`: Memory read mode. One of `read`, `list`, or `search`.
- `MEMORY_WRITE`
  - `detail_type`: Always `MEMORY_WRITE`.
  - `agent_id`: Identifier for the agent.
  - `version_id`: Identifier for the runtime version.
  - `run_id`: Stable runtime identifier used to correlate later activity for the same run.
  - `memory_path`: Memory file path relative to the agent Memory root.
  - `access_method`: Memory write mode. One of `create` or `update`.
- `SKILL_USED`
  - `detail_type`: Always `SKILL_USED`.
  - `agent_id`: Identifier for the agent.
  - `version_id`: Identifier for the runtime version.
  - `run_id`: Stable runtime identifier used to correlate later activity for the same run.
  - `skill_id`: Identifier for the attached skill on the agent version.
  - `skill_name`: Display name of the attached skill.
  - `skill_type`: Skill source type. One of `uploaded_skill` or `chatgpt_skill_ref`.
- `TRIGGER_CREATED`
  - `detail_type`: Always `TRIGGER_CREATED`.
  - `agent_id`: Identifier for the agent.
  - `trigger_id`: Identifier for the trigger.
  - `trigger_type`: Trigger type string.
  - `trigger_fields`: Sanitized trigger snapshot. Connector triggers expose connector_id, link_id, webhook_name, required_actions, enabled, instructions, and param_keys only.
- `TRIGGER_DELETED`
  - `detail_type`: Always `TRIGGER_DELETED`.
  - `agent_id`: Identifier for the agent.
  - `trigger_id`: Identifier for the trigger.
  - `trigger_type`: Trigger type string.
  - `trigger_fields`: Sanitized pre-delete trigger snapshot.
- `TRIGGER_UPDATED`
  - `detail_type`: Always `TRIGGER_UPDATED`.
  - `agent_id`: Identifier for the agent.
  - `trigger_id`: Identifier for the trigger.
  - `trigger_type`: Trigger type string.
  - `trigger_fields`: Sanitized trigger snapshot.

Connector and Memory metadata is curated for compliance export. Secret values, connector params, link params, scopes, OAuth client IDs, labels, raw command text, absolute workspace paths, and file contents are excluded.

tags.name: Costs
tags.description:
This section describes COSTS log files as available through the OpenAI Compliance Logs Platform.

List COSTS files with `GET /v1/compliance/organizations/{organization_id}/logs`
and `event_type=COSTS`. Use the API Platform organization ID; COSTS is not
available from the workspace logs route.

The expected latency for COSTS data is 3-5 hours.

Each COSTS entry captures one paid-plan usage and billing row for one UTC hour. Use these records for reporting and warehouse ingestion; they follow the source paid-plan credits reporting table rather than request-time billing semantics.

`event_type` = `COSTS`
Fine-grained API key scope: `chatgpt.enterprise.compliance_logs_platform.costs.read`.
API keys with `chatgpt.enterprise.compliance_logs_platform.read` or the legacy
`chatgpt.enterprise.compliance_export.read` scope can also read Costs.

#### Schema
Each event conforms to the shared Logs Platform envelope described above with these additional fields:
- `type`: Always `COSTS`.
- `principal`: The organization that owns the usage. COSTS events are emitted with an `API_PLATFORM_ORG` principal.
- `actor`: A system actor for the COSTS exporter.
- `payload`: Object with the cost usage and billing fields for the reporting hour.
  - `day`: UTC reporting date in `YYYY-MM-DD` format.
  - `hour`: UTC reporting hour from `0` through `23`.
  - `organization_id`: OpenAI organization identifier for the billed organization.
  - `identity`: User or agent identity associated with the usage when user or agent attribution is available.
    - `user_id`: Public user identifier when user attribution is available.
    - `email`: User email address when profile enrichment is available.
    - `name`: User display name when profile enrichment is available.
    - `groups`: Workspace groups associated with the usage. Group membership is part of the COSTS grain, so different membership combinations produce separate entries. Each group contains:
      - `id`: Workspace group identifier.
      - `name`: Current workspace group name, or `null` when the group no longer exists or its name cannot be resolved.
    - `agent`: Workspace Agent associated with the usage when agent attribution is available.
      - `id`: Workspace Agent ID from paid-plans usage attribution.
      - `name`: Current Workspace Agent name when metadata is available.
  - `product`: Product or origin associated with the usage.
  - `surface`: Surface associated with the activity.
  - `client`: Client associated with the activity.
  - `model`: Model associated with the usage when available.
  - `service_tier`: Service tier associated with the usage when available.
  - `reasoning`: Reasoning effort or tier associated with the usage when available.
  - `measures`: Usage and billing measures for the row.

COSTS usage, product, and measure fields are emitted directly on `payload`. User and agent attribution are nested under `payload.identity`; COSTS does not add a separate `dimensions` or resource hierarchy.

#### Measures
The `measures` object contains:
- `usage`: Token usage associated with the row. Depending on the exact nature of your plan type you will be presented with either detailed fields such as `text_cached_input_tokens` or with totals such as `text_total_tokens`.
- `billing`: Array of SKU charge entries. Each entry contains:
  - `sku`: Customer-visible SKU name.
  - `quantity`: Object with `value` and `unit`.
  - `cost`: Object with `value` and `unit`.
  - `estimated_cost_usd`: Optional object with `value` and `unit`. Populated only when the SKU has a `cost` in `CREDITS`. Calculated from the most recent USD credit overage price available when the event is generated.

#### Usage fields
Detailed token usage fields may include:
- `text_input_tokens`
- `text_cached_input_tokens`
- `text_output_tokens`
- `audio_input_tokens`
- `audio_cached_input_tokens`
- `audio_output_tokens`
- `image_input_tokens`
- `image_cached_input_tokens`
- `image_output_tokens`

Total-only token usage fields may include:
- `text_total_tokens`
- `audio_total_tokens`
- `image_total_tokens`

#### Example
```json
{
  "event_id": "70dfe00c-2852-43f4-a52b-8f61113f16c9",
  "type": "COSTS",
  "timestamp": "2026-03-10T13:59:59Z",
  "principal": {
    "id": "org-XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX",
    "type": "API_PLATFORM_ORG"
  },
  "actor": {
    "type": "SYSTEM",
    "id": "costs_compliance"
  },
  "payload": {
    "day": "2026-03-10",
    "hour": 13,
    "organization_id": "org-XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX",
    "identity": {
      "user_id": "user-XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX",
      "email": "user@example.com",
      "name": "Alex Example",
      "groups": [
        {
          "id": "0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef",
          "name": "Platform"
        }
      ],
      "agent": {
        "id": "agt_123",
        "name": "Procurement Review Agent"
      }
    },
    "product": "chatgpt",
    "surface": "chatgpt",
    "client": "web",
    "model": "gpt-5.5",
    "service_tier": "default",
    "reasoning": "medium",
    "measures": {
      "usage": {
        "text_input_tokens": 1000,
        "text_cached_input_tokens": 90000,
        "image_output_tokens": 1500
      },
      "billing": [
        {
          "sku": "chat.completion.5.reasoning",
          "quantity": {
            "value": 1000,
            "unit": "tokens"
          },
          "cost": {
            "value": 5,
            "unit": "CREDITS"
          },
          "estimated_cost_usd": {
            "value": 0.2,
            "unit": "USD"
          }
        },
        {
          "sku": "chat.completion.5.cached_input",
          "quantity": {
            "value": 90000,

          },
          "cost": {
            "value": 15,

          },
          "estimated_cost_usd": {

          }
        }

    }

}
```

tags.description:
These endpoints provide time-indexed exports for workspace entities (e.g. users, GPTs, projects, files, etc) of the current state at request time.

The APIs are designed for regularly downloading data diffs to synchronize an offline database for data compliance, rather than mass export. The initial data sync will take longer, but subsequent syncs will be faster as only the diffs need to be downloaded. The API is rate limited to prevent abuse.

In general new datatypes will be exposed using the OpenAI Compliance Logs Platform events as opposed to new Stateful endpoints.

Endpoints for listing ChatGPT Enterprise workspace groups, listing group users, and adding or removing users from manually managed groups.

Use these endpoints when you need current workspace group state for access reviews, data governance, or admin workflow automation. List endpoints support cursor pagination with a default page size of 20 and a maximum page size of 100.
